parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Kenpoly-sec-school-field, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1874 | 2.78 | 2.78
2 | 2428 | 9.13 | 11.9
3 | 1071 | 15.2 | 27.1
4 | 3706 | 32.2 | 59.3
5 | 178 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KHK-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Kenpoly-sec-school-field, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report — Station Kenpoly-sec-school-field, Bori Metropolis**

The VES interpretation yields a five-layer resistivity sequence: 1874 Ω·m (0–2.78 m), 2428 Ω·m (2.78–11.9 m), 1071 Ω·m (11.9–27.1 m), 3706 Ω·m (27.1–59.3 m), and 178 Ω·m (basement/substratum, >59.3 m). Resistivity rises from layer 1 to 2, drops sharply to layer 3, rises again to a high-resistivity layer 4, then falls markedly to a low-resistivity layer 5 — consistent with alternating resistive and conductive units overlying a conductive basal layer, possibly indicating a confined aquifer zone within layer 3 or 5.

Applying the standard curve-type convention to the three successive triplets (1-2-3, 2-3-4, 3-4-5) gives K, H, K respectively, confirming the on-file classification of **KHK-type**. The classification is consistent with the resistivity-depth profile and requires no revision.

{"curve_type_stated": "KHK", "label_issue_flagged": false}
